label: Isolation & confinement
description: Always on, and grows with mission length. Acts mostly upstream through stress, plus a direct immune effect from meeting fewer new microbes.

label: Psychological stress
description: The most useful factor to monitor: it varies day to day and reaches immune, muscle, bone, vessels and glucose through cortisol. Trackable with HRV, sleep and saliva cortisol.

label: Space radiation
description: Varies with solar events and is already tracked by dosimeters. Hits lymphocytes, bone and, in deep space, blood vessels.
varies_day_to_day: Yes: spikes with solar particle events

label: Microgravity
description: The biggest cause in the map (muscle, bone, heart, direct immune effect, and it amplifies stress). Because it never changes, track its variable version: exercise and loading logs.

label: Cortisol / HPA axis
description: Stress hormone hub (with DHEA). Connects stress to immune suppression, muscle breakdown, bone resorption and insulin resistance.

label: Inflammation / oxidative stress
description: The main hub. Shared signalling molecules (IL-6, RANKL, TNF-α) link the immune system, bone, muscle and blood vessels. Radiation and unloading both raise oxidative stress.

label: Fluid shift
description: Blood moves toward the head: puffy face, headache, stuffy head, flu-like feeling. Changes HR, HRV and BP baselines and can look like illness, so it confounds several signals.

label: Unloading / inactivity
description: No weight-bearing, so muscle, bone and heart shrink together. Inactivity also makes muscle about 3× more sensitive to cortisol.

label: Exercise & loading
description: The one countermeasure that protects muscle, bone and heart together. Fully offsets cardiac atrophy; only slows muscle and bone loss.

label: Immune dysregulation
description: About 50% of astronauts. White-cell counts look normal, but T-cell and NK-cell function drops and plasma cytokines rise. Lasts the whole 6-month mission. NASA: still unclear whether it causes more disease.

label: Insulin resistance (glucose)
description: Fasting insulin was elevated in flight in all astronauts (CSA Vascular). Bed rest plus high cortisol: leg insulin sensitivity 9.1 → 5.2 mg/kg/min. CGMs already used in space research.

label: Bone loss
description: Osteoclasts dominate: resorption up, formation down. Hit from four directions: unloading, radiation, cortisol and inflammation (RANKL).

label: Muscle loss
description: Atrophy continues despite exercise programmes. Muscle also signals back to immunity through myokines such as IL-6.

label: Heart & blood pressure
description: HR up, BP down ~10 mmHg, HRV down. Left-ventricle mass −12% after a short flight. A smaller heart can still be healthy (normal adaptation vs a problem). Fainting on standing after landing.

label: Blood vessels
description: Real risk for deep space (Apollo data, mouse radiation studies), but in low Earth orbit arteries showed no thickening or stiffening over 5 years.

label: Latent virus reactivation
description: EBV, VZV, CMV and HSV-1 shed by 53% of shuttle and 61% of ISS astronauts. Rises with mission length. Mostly without symptoms.

label: Illness & symptoms
description: ISS records: skin rashes 1.12 per flight-year, upper respiratory 0.97. 46% of crew had a notable event. In one shingles case vital signs stayed normal, so symptom logging matters.

label: Wearables (Astroskin, ARCHeR)
description: Already flown: Astroskin smart shirt on ISS since 2018 (ECG, BP, SpO₂, breathing, skin temp, activity), Garmin on Polaris Dawn, ARCHeR wristbands on Artemis II. Hardware is mostly solved; the software that fuses signals is the gap.

label: Camera rPPG (RGB + NIR)
description: Contact-free HR, HRV and breathing from facial colour changes. RGB+NIR fusion is most robust. Not yet validated on astronauts in orbit: an opportunity. Hackathon-friendly with a webcam and rPPG-Toolbox.

label: Mission day count
description: Free proxy for isolation load and for viral reactivation risk, which grows with mission length.

label: Saliva cortisol + viral DNA
description: Reads the stress → virus chain directly. Needs a lab, but saliva is easy to collect; used on ISS and Artemis II.

label: Sweat cortisol
description: Direct hormone reading, but only prototypes; some need visible sweat; not tested in space.

label: CGM (glucose)
description: Continuous glucose monitors are already used in space health research.

label: Symptom log
description: Rash, sore throat, fatigue. Open question: how to collect it without annoying a busy crew.

label: Facial behaviour change
description: Faces are not reliable emotion readers; drop micro-expressions. Useful only as one input in fusion, as change from the person’s own baseline. Frame as medical/safety under the EU AI Act; crew own their data.

label: Blood pressure
description: Stress raises it ~7 mmHg, but spaceflight lowers it ~10 mmHg. Weak stress signal.

label: HRV (ECG / PPG)
description: Stress shifts it toward sympathetic, and that response is unchanged in space. Baseline is lowered by microgravity, so compare to the astronaut’s own in-flight baseline.

label: Resting HR vs own baseline
description: Smartwatch study: 63% of COVID cases flaggable before symptoms; LSTM autoencoder (LAAD) flagged 92%. Catches symptomatic infection, not silent viral shedding.

label: Sleep (actigraphy)
description: Astronauts average ~6 h vs 8.5 h scheduled; ~75% used sleep meds. Both a cause and a symptom of stress.

label: Scans & strength tests
description: Only way to see muscle and bone change, and it is slow. No daily reading.

label: Exercise / loading log
description: The variable version of microgravity: how much loading each astronaut actually got.

label: Radiation dosimeter
description: Already exists on every mission; captures dose spikes from solar events.

label: Sympathetic / autonomic nervous system
description: The stress system lives in the brain: amygdala → hypothalamus → both the HPA axis (cortisol) and the sympathetic nervous system. Sympathetic responses dominate after short flights; cortisol-driven changes dominate after longer ones. HRV is a direct read-out of this system.

label: Brain structure & CSF
description: Brain shifts upward in the skull; ventricles enlarge ~11–25%. Growth slows after ~6 months and recovers only partly 6–12 months after landing. Crews with <3 years between missions showed little further enlargement. Medical meaning still unclear.

label: Eyes (SANS)
description: Spaceflight-associated neuro-ocular syndrome: optic disc edema, globe flattening, choroidal folds, hyperopic shift. ~81% of NASA long-duration astronauts had at least one finding; ~66% show the earliest sign. So far vision effects have been correctable with glasses.

label: Balance & motion sickness (vestibular)
description: Sensory mismatch in microgravity: ~70% of astronauts have space motion sickness or impaired motor performance, mostly resolving within 1 h to 4 days. Re-entry motion sickness is worse after long missions and does not reliably improve with repeat flights.

label: Cognition & performance
description: 25 ISS astronauts: no systematic decline on 6-month missions. Early flight: slower processing speed, visual working memory, sustained attention. Late flight: slower emotion recognition. Processing speed recovered only after return.

label: Cognition test battery
description: Computerised tests (Cognition battery, WinSCAT). WinSCAT is a medical requirement for US long-duration crew.

label: Eye imaging (OCT)
description: Optical coherence tomography detects optic disc edema and globe changes; in-flight imaging and AI detection are improving.

label: Brain MRI
description: Only pre- and post-flight; not available in orbit.

label: EVA (spacewalk)
description: Extravehicular activity causes acute physical load, sleep disruption, and elevated stress hormones linked to latent viral reactivation.
